title: feat(spec/ai): blueprint select options declare their lifecycle kind and a blueprint object names its stageField
body:
Fixes #24198

Clause-②: yes

## What changed

The object schema already requires a lifecycle `kind` (`open` / `won` / `lost`) on every option of the field an object's `stageField` names (`refuseStageFieldWithoutKinds`, `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`). The AI blueprint had no slot for either key, so the design model could not say which field is an object's stage or which option ends its lifecycle, and that rule never applied to an AI-built object. Both blueprint shapes now carry both keys (`packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts`):

| Key | Lenient (`SolutionBlueprintSchema`, what `apply_blueprint` parses) | Strict mirror (`SolutionBlueprintStrictSchema`, the structured-output contract) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `fields[].options[].kind` | optional | required, nullable |
| `objects[].stageField` | optional, `SNAKE_CASE` | required, nullable, `SNAKE_CASE` (`strictIdentOrNull`, the same as `nameField`) |

- **`kind` reuses `SelectOption.kind`'s enum by identity.** One shared reference, `optionKindEnum()`, reads `SelectOptionSchema.shape.kind.unwrap()`. Each side then adds its own form of "optional" (`.optional()` on the lenient side, `.nullable()` on the strict side). The three values are written nowhere in this file. `field.zod.ts` is not edited, and `SelectOption`'s accept set does not change. It is a function, not a module-level constant, so the lenient lazy shapes do not force `SelectOptionSchema` at import.
- **`stageField` sits next to `nameField`** in both object shapes and maps onto `ObjectSchema.stageField`. Only the string form is carried. The object schema's `false` ("no linear lifecycle") has no blueprint spelling (see Acceptance notes).
- **The describes are written from `refuseStageFieldWithoutKinds`, not from the card.** One shared sentence (`STAGE_FIELD_RULE`) appears in all four describes. It says the object schema refuses the object unless the named field is a single-value `select` or `radio` whose inline options each declare `kind`, and that naming a multiselect / checkboxes / tags field that carries options is refused too. The option describes add the `FieldSchema` half: `kind` only goes on a single-value `select` / `radio` field's options.
- Regenerated by their generators: `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json` (+`ai/BlueprintObject:stageField`) and `content/docs/references/ai/solution-blueprint.mdx`. The published `json-schema/ai/SolutionBlueprintStrict.json` is gitignored and built by `gen:schema`. After the build it has both keys, and every object node's `required` still equals its `properties` with `additionalProperties: false` (checked by walking the built file).
- Changeset `.changeset/24198-blueprint-option-kind-stage-field.md`: `@objectstack/spec` `minor`.

## Premise checks (on `origin/main` `f792290df`, this branch's base)

- **No key existed before.** `grep -n "kind\|stageField\|nameField"` over `solution-blueprint.zod.ts` found `stageField` 0 times and no `kind` key. The only `kind` hits were two describe strings that say "View kind". Control: `nameField` hit at `:109` and `:358`.
- **`ObjectSchema.stageField` is the only trigger of the mandatory-kind rule.** `git grep refuseStageFieldWithoutKinds` gives one definition (`object.zod.ts:1970`), one call (`:3160`, with `object.stageField`), one docblock mention and the liveness note. No `stageField` is declared anywhere in `packages/spec/src` other than `object.zod.ts:2897`. The non-spec readers of `stageField` (lint `validate-semantic-roles`, `validate-object-field-refs`, metadata-core FLS references, metadata-protocol reference sites) check that the pointer resolves. None of them requires `kind`. So `stageField` rides this card, as the seat's ruling said it would if this premise held.
- **No consumer outside `packages/spec`.** `git grep -E "SolutionBlueprintStrictSchema|SolutionBlueprintSchema" -- ':!packages/spec/**'` gave 5 hits: a consumed changeset, the auto-generated reference page and ADR-0033. None is code. Control: the same names hit 70 times in `solution-blueprint.test.ts` and 11 times in `solution-blueprint.zod.ts`. The consumer is cloud's `propose_blueprint` / `apply_blueprint` (objectstack-ai/cloud#2926).

## Tests

`packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.test.ts`, 72 tests:

- **Lenient:** both keys survive the parse; both stay optional; `kind` is `SelectOptionSchema.shape.kind.unwrap()` itself, on both sides (identity, not shape); a `kind` outside the vocabulary is refused at `objects.0.fields.1.options.2.kind`; a non-snake_case `stageField` is refused at `objects.0.stageField`. A contract leg copies a parsed blueprint object 1:1 into `ObjectSchema`. It parses, and once one option drops its `kind`, the object schema refuses it at exactly `fields.status.options.3.kind` (`custom`).
- **Strict:** both keys are carried; null is accepted for both; leaving either key out is refused at exactly its own path; an off-vocabulary `kind` and a non-snake_case `stageField` are refused.
- **Parity:** a new option-level key-parity pin (both sides equal `['kind', 'label', 'value']`). The object-level pin now names `stageField`.
- **Existing strict fixtures** gained `stageField: null` and, where they carry options, `kind: null`. Without that, the leading-digit pin would have stayed red because a new key was missing rather than because of the digit.

Results at `5645c2cd9` (the merge of `origin/main` `f7af83945`):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: 691 files, 20974 passed, 1 todo, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` (tsc, scripts and the test-layer program, which compiles `src/**/*.test.ts`): exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build && pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`: all 14 generated artifacts up to date, exit 0.

**Ablation**, run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. Each anchor hit once, the blob changed, and the restore was proven (blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty). The test reads `src` directly, so no build or dist step is involved.

- Strict `stageField` renamed to `stageFieldAblated`: 20 failed / 52 passed, including `the OBJECT schemas carry exactly the same keys`.
- Lenient option `kind` renamed to `kindAblated`: 5 failed / 67 passed. The failures are the option key-parity pin, the carry test, the identity test, the vocabulary refusal and the `ObjectSchema` contract leg.

The direction was red both times, as predicted.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 108 commands for this diff, and all were run at `5645c2cd9`. `--ran` reconciliation: **108 derived, 107 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**.

- NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`. Family: dual-build CJS loads. Reason: exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET, because it needs a whole-workspace `pnpm build`. This is a declared narrowing, and CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs it.
- Six gates first answered exit 3 or a stale reading. A concurrent `turbo` build of `@objectstack/lint` rebuilt `packages/spec/dist` while they ran, so their first answers measured nothing. Once lint, formula and objectql were built, all 13 gates in the overlap window were re-run, and all exited 0: `check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:doc-security-posture`, spec `check:exported-any`, `check:generated`, `check:liveness`, `check:llms-txt`, `check:skill-examples`, `check:skill-refs`, `check:strictness-ledger`, `check:variant-docs`, `check:yaml-examples`, `check:changeset-gate-self-tests` and `check:lean-entry-closure`.
- Not run locally because CI owns them: the repo-wide scans, `test:repo`, the workspace and consumer type-check lanes, Test Core, Build Core and dogfood.

## Acceptance notes

- **`stageField: false` has no blueprint spelling.** `ObjectSchema.stageField` also takes `false`, which declares a status field non-linear and turns off stage heuristics. The card scopes `stageField` as a snake_case name, and no producer or consumer of `false` from the blueprint is named, so only the string form is carried. Owner: none. Noted, not filed.
- **The blueprint does not judge kinds itself.** Strict structured output cannot express a rule that spans keys ("every option of the field `stageField` names has a non-null `kind`"). The refusal arrives, located, when the applier writes the object through `ObjectSchema` (pinned by the contract leg above). The describes tell the model the rule up front.
- **Cloud seam (objectstack-ai/cloud#2926):** `apply_blueprint` copies `objects[].stageField` onto the object and `options[].kind` onto each option, after stripping the strict mirror's nulls to absent, as it does for every other key. The renderer half is objectstack-ai/objectui#12907.
